text:
Incident-Bot: :rotating_light: P1 detected in prod-us-east-1. High rate of cudaMalloc failures for kv-cache allocations on redwood/gpt-rt-quant-canary. Triggering page to oncall. thread_ts=1780123456

Sam (oncall): Got it. Looking at alerts now. p95 token latency spiking and request retries increasing. Anyone seeing 5xxs?

Kai (runtime): 502s are cropping up as retries exhaust. Trend: continuous batching workload with lots of short prefixes is producing many small KV cache allocations; over 30-40 minutes we see fragmentation and then malloc failures for larger contiguous allocations (cold syncs, cache repop).

Priya (sre): Stack snippet from node-7g:
```
[2026-03-01T03:12:07Z] WARN model=redwood/gpt-rt-quant-canary allocator: fragmentation_ratio=0.72 largest_free_block_mb=24 free_total_mb=512
[2026-03-01T03:12:11Z] ERROR cuda: cudaMalloc returned out of memory while allocating 256MB
[2026-03-01T03:12:12Z] WARN request_id=abc123 fallback path executed, latency_ms=1805
```

Marcos (infra): I can push a config update to the runtime pool. Options: tweak PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF, reduce continuous_batching window, or temporarily set dynamic_kv=false to force recompute rather than many tiny KV allocations. Which to try first?

Kai (runtime): Quickest low-risk: set PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64 and reduce continuous_batching.max_concurrent_prefixes from 32 -> 8 for the affected model in us-east-1. That should reduce large contiguous allocation requests and encourage smaller splits in allocator.

Sam (oncall): Patch and canary please. Also start routing 15% of traffic to a fallback non-quantized build to relieve pressure.

Marcos (infra): Running rctl patch:
```
rctl model update redwood/gpt-rt-quant-canary --region us-east-1 \
  --set continuous_batching.max_concurrent_prefixes=8 \
  --env PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF="max_split_size_mb:64"
```
Deploying to 6 instances as a canary.

SRE-Bot: Deployment triggered by Marcos at 2026-03-01T03:15:14Z. Canary=6 pods. Rollout strategy: gradual.

Alex (cs): We have two dedicated customers (acct-774, acct-998) reporting increased tails. CS reaching out with note and ETA.

Priya (sre): Observing metrics: within 90s of canary deploy, cudaMalloc failures in canary group dropped 90%. p99 latency for canary traffic from ~2.1s -> 140ms. Overall cluster still noisy; will watch.

Kai (runtime): I'll keep continuous monitoring. If canary is stable for 10 minutes, propose rolling to 50% then full. Also propose adding a runtime flag to auto-fallback continuous_batching when fragmentation_ratio > 0.6 for quantized models.

Sam (oncall): Noting timeline: pager @03:13, mitigation started @03:15. Will keep incident open until full rollout and CS confirmations.

Marcos (infra): Rolling to 50% now. Also enabling temporary alert: fragmentation_ratio > 0.6 -> page infra and auto-set continuous_batching.max_concurrent_prefixes=4 for that model.

Priya (sre): Side investigation: reproducer showed fragmentation occurs faster when quantization patch Q2 was enabled (reduced per-key buffer packing). I'm starting a bisect to isolate which commit introduced the allocation pattern.

Kai (runtime): Long-term fixes to consider: 1) allocator arena tuning (reduce max chunk size, increase coalescing), 2) pre-reserve contiguous arenas for large KV writes, 3) smarter batching that groups prefixes to avoid many small concurrent KV allocations.

Alex (cs): CS update: both accounts were informed; one asked for a brief timeline and escalation path, they've accepted the mitigation pending the postmortem.

Sam (oncall): Canary healthy at 50% for 8 minutes. No new OOMs in canary. Rolling remaining 50% now.

SRE-Bot: Rollout completed at 2026-03-01T03:29:10Z. All instances now have PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64 and reduced concurrent_prefixes.

Sam (oncall): Full cluster metrics show cudaMalloc error rate back to baseline, p99 latency stabilizing ~110-160ms. Marking incident as mitigated. Handoff to follow-up owners.

Priya (sre): Creating incident ticket INC-2026-03-01-kv-alloc-frag for postmortem. Assigning owners: Priya (SRE) + Kai (runtime) + Marcos (infra).

Kai (runtime): Postmortem action items I/O:
- Reproduce in staging with stress harness to confirm allocator tuning helps.
- Add per-model allocator env and UI control.
- Implement auto-disable of continuous_batching for quantized variants if fragmentation_ratio crosses threshold.

Marcos (infra): Infra tasks:
- Experiment with PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF defaults (64, 128, 256) on canary.
- Add metric largest_free_block_mb and fragmentation_ratio to console dashboards.

Priya (sre): Priya will own customer impact summary and signal when compensations are needed. CS to prepare outreach.

Alex (cs): CS follow-up scheduled for 09:00 PT tomorrow with affected customers.

Sam (oncall): Handoff notes for next oncall:
- Current state: mitigations applied globally in us-east-1. No active OOMs for 40m.
- Customers: acct-774 and acct-998 impacted; CS handling comms.
- Further investigation: bisect quantization changes, test allocator knob values in staging.

SRE-Bot: Incident INC-2026-03-01-kv-alloc-frag marked mitigated at 2026-03-01T03:40:10Z. Postmortem owner: Priya (sre).

Marcos (infra): Quick note: if fragmentation recurs after rollback, we should consider temporarily disabling caching for this model until allocator fixes land.

Kai (runtime): I'll take the handoff. Running staged reproducer with different max_split_size_mb values and will report findings in the incident ticket.

Sam (oncall): Thanks team. Closing console thread, handing off to Kai and Priya for follow-up.
